summary: The same claim as a-clock-nobody-shares-is-not-a-start, driven through the real orchestrator, event log, Rental Schedule, and Run Bundle. One Run and one machine, and the machine's wall clock runs an hour ahead of Mercator's. It holds the whole image assembled and idle, so the only stages left are the container starting and the application coming up, and twenty seconds after the launch is taken its runtime hands back a process. Asked about it, the host states that start on the clock it has, an hour in Mercator's future, alongside its own read of now on the same clock: the two agree with each other and neither agrees with anything the control plane knows. Mercator adopts neither. The run stream records no start, the Run Bundle's start-latency row says start_not_observed rather than filing 3600 seconds as a measurement, and the Booking's enforced runtime is measured from the read that carried the observation, so the machine comes free when the capacity is really spent. What this fixture holds that the placement corpus cannot is the standing law over a real execution: safety.start_is_observed_not_inferred reads both the run stream and the schedule here, rather than a record a test wrote by hand.
